summary: Gated by payment. You can create an X app and enable OAuth 2.0 in the developer console without review. Every API call draws down prepaid credits, so there is no useful free usage. Budget per request: third-party breakdowns put post reads at about $0.005 and a post containing a link at $0.20. Watch the 30-second authorization-code expiry.

oauth_support_claim.text: X supports OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code with PKCE (X API v2), and OAuth 1.0a.
oauth_support_claim.quote: OAuth 2.0 can be used with the X API v2 only.

difficulty_claim.text: No review blocks you, but API access is pay-per-usage with prepaid credits, so a payment method and a usage budget are required before your agent can do anything useful.
difficulty_claim.quote: The X API uses pay-per-usage pricing.
difficulty_claim.note: The official page refused automated fetch (HTTP 403). Quote from a search snippet of docs.x.com.

claim.text: Not confirmed. Even with a managed app, someone pays for X API usage. Check how Composio bills X calls.
claim.note: Set COMPOSIO_API_KEY and regenerate to check the live catalog.

endpoints.note: Common X OAuth 2.0 endpoints, not tested live. The fetched docs page did not show the URLs in text.

hands_on.text: 20-40 minutes (developer account, app, OAuth 2.0 settings, credits)

approval_wait.text: No app review found in the docs. Paying for credits is the gate.
approval_wait.note: No review step appears in the sources checked. Enterprise access goes through an interest form with no published price.

fastest_path.text: Buy a small credit balance, cap auto-recharge, and test with your own account first.

steps.title: Sign up in the X developer console
steps.detail: Accept the developer terms and describe your use case.
steps.note: The console refused automated access (HTTP 403), so the flow was not walked.

steps.title: Enable OAuth 2.0 and pick 'Web App' (confidential client)
steps.detail: Web App and Automated App/bot are confidential clients and get a client secret. Native and single-page apps are public clients.
steps.quote: Native App and Single page Apps are public clients and Web App and Automated App or bots are confidential clients.

steps.title: Add the exact Composio callback URL
steps.detail: X validates the redirect URI with exact matching.
steps.quote: For OAuth 2.0, you will need to have exact match validation for your callback URL.

steps.title: Request offline.access with your scopes
steps.detail: Without offline.access there is no refresh token, and access tokens last two hours.
steps.quote: If this scope is not passed, we will not generate a refresh token.

steps.title: Add a card and buy credits
steps.detail: Credits are deducted per request. Track usage in the Developer Console.
steps.note: From a search snippet of docs.x.com.

steps.title: Estimate cost per agent action
steps.detail: Third-party breakdowns: about $0.005 per post read, $0.010 per user read, $0.015 per post created, $0.20 for a post with a URL, with reads capped at 3M a month on pay-per-use.
steps.note: Third-party sources only. Check the prices in your console.

gotchas.title: Authorization codes expire in 30 seconds
gotchas.detail: Exchange the code for a token immediately. Slow callbacks or queued workers will fail.
gotchas.quote: The auth_code has a time limit of 30 seconds

gotchas.title: Access tokens last 2 hours
gotchas.detail: Unless you request offline.access and refresh.
gotchas.quote: will only stay valid for two hours unless you’ve used the offline.access scope

gotchas.title: Posts with links cost much more
gotchas.detail: Third-party sources say a post containing a URL costs about 13x a plain post.

blockers.title: Cost at scale
blockers.detail: Read-heavy agents (monitoring, search) get expensive, and pay-per-use is capped at 3M post reads a month.
blockers.workaround: Cache aggressively, read only what you need, and contact X for Enterprise above the cap.

conflicts.resolution: Treat any free credit as a promotion. Check the console.
